scenarios.description: Drive 2 perfectly formatted packets from reset in HUNT mode and observe sync_locked asserting high on the cycle following the second packet's completion.

In LOCKED mode, inject a single-bit error in the checksum byte of a 5-byte payload packet and verify that out_err asserts at out_eop, pkt_count does not increment, err_count increments by 1, and sync_locked remains 1.
In LOCKED mode, drive two consecutive packets with length violations (>16 bytes) and verify that out_err asserts on each and sync_locked drops to 0 after the second frame.
Drive back-to-back valid packets with 0 idle cycles between EOP and SOP while locked, verifying unbroken 1-cycle pipeline forwarding and accurate pkt_count increments.
Assert synchronous rst_n mid-packet in LOCKED mode and verify that sync_locked drops to 0, out_valid immediately drops to 0, and internal counters reset to 0.
Drive an alternating pattern of 1 valid packet followed by 1 corrupted packet repeatedly in LOCKED mode to verify that lock is maintained due to single-error hysteresis.

requirements.description: A valid packet structure consists of 1 SOP byte (which serves as the length field N, where 1 <= N <= 16), followed by exactly N payload bytes, followed by 1 checksum byte marked with rx_eop.
The checksum byte must equal the cumulative bitwise XOR of the SOP length byte and all N payload bytes.
In HUNT mode (sync_locked=0), out_valid, out_sop, out_eop, and out_err must remain continuously 0.
Transition from HUNT to LOCKED requires 2 consecutive valid error-free packets without any interleaving framing violations or checksum errors.
While sync_locked=1, incoming bytes are registered and emitted on out_data, out_sop, out_eop, and out_valid exactly 1 clock cycle after arrival when rx_valid=1.
If a frame error (payload length mismatch, unexpected SOP while in packet, missing EOP, or XOR checksum mismatch) occurs while sync_locked=1, out_err must assert high synchronously with out_eop.
If 2 consecutive corrupted packets occur while sync_locked=1, sync_locked must deassert to 0 on the cycle following the second corrupted packet's EOP.
pkt_count increments by 1 on each out_eop where out_err is 0, and err_count increments on every corrupted frame EOP (or abort cycle).
rx_sop and rx_eop are only sampled and acted upon when rx_valid is high.
rx_sop must not assert when a packet is already in progress before rx_eop has arrived.
rx_eop must not assert on the same cycle as rx_sop (minimum frame size is 3 bytes: SOP, 1 Payload, EOP).
When sync_locked is asserted, every asserted rx_valid creates an out_valid pulse exactly 1 cycle later.
out_sop and out_eop must never assert when out_valid is low.
out_err must never assert unless out_eop and out_valid are simultaneously high.
All SystemVerilog assertions compile cleanly without syntax errors and bind correctly to frame_sync_packet_validator.
Properties rigorously verify lock acquisition timing, loss of lock hysteresis, checksum correctness, pipeline latency, and error flag containment.
Assertions check both positive valid packet forwarding and negative error-flag assertion without false positives during unaligned or hunting phases.
